channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: United Kingdom: BoE holds but risks later cuts – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s UK team notes weakening housing demand as mortgage approvals fall to late-2023 lows, while business lending remains firm and wage expectations show limited second-round effects.

item.title: Gold bears retain control as Fed hike bets and Oil-driven inflation weigh
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades with a modest downside bias during American trading hours on Monday. A softer US Dollar (USD) limits the decline and helps the metal recover part of its earlier losses.

item.title: Australian Dollar hits three-month high as RBA rate hike bets intensify
item.description: AUD/USD advances on Monday, gaining 0.22% on the day to trade around 0.7220 at the time of writing, after reaching its highest level in more than three months.

item.title: WTI Oil climbs as Middle East supply risks remain evelated
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil edges higher on Monday as fresh attacks by the United States and Iran over the weekend add to already elevated supply concerns from the months-long war in the Middle East. At the time of writing, WTI trades around $91.15 per barrel, its highest level since July 24.

item.title: Japanese Yen: September BoJ decision shapes path – HSBC
item.description: HSBC highlights that markets now expect the Bank of Japan (BoJ) to tighten policy more quickly, with overnight index swaps implying about 75bp of cumulative hikes by April 2027 and assigning odds to a move at the 18 September meeting.

item.title: Bank of Canada: Rates outlook and inflation risks – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists Robert Both and Emma Lawrence highlight that the Bank of Canada adopted a more hawkish tone, emphasizing upside inflation risks even as core inflation stays subdued.

item.title: Eurozone: Resilient growth, worrying inflation – ABN AMRO
item.description: ABN AMRO economists Bill Diviney and Jan-Paul van de Kerke expect Eurozone growth to remain resilient despite a renewed energy shock, supported by German fiscal spending and solid underlying activity.

item.title: United Kingdom: Growth pace cools after hot start – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank economists Sanjay Raja and Maui Brennan expect United Kingdom (UK) Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to have slipped slightly in July after strong growth earlier in 2026. They forecast a modest monthly contraction led by services and production, with construction only marginally higher.

item.title: US Dollar: CPI outcome to steer Fed path – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes the US Dollar (USD) weakened on broad Japanese Yen strength before partially recovering as strong US August payrolls revived expectations for a September Fed hike.

item.title: Gold: Bull market conviction broadens – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts Michael Haigh and Jeremy Sellem describe a broad-based Gold bull market in 2026, driven by ETFs, futures and options positioning. They highlight strong physical ETF inflows, near-record futures exposure by money managers and a structurally bullish options skew.

item.title: Japanese Yen hits six-and-a-half-month high on hawkish BoJ bets
item.description: USD/JPY extends its steep decline on Monday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) rallies against the US Dollar (USD), supported by hawkish Bank of Japan (BoJ) expectations, capital repatriation and the unwinding of Yen-funded carry trades.

item.title: United States: Inflation risks but still contained - TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities projects August Core CPI at 0.19% m/m and 2.3% y/y, with services driving gains and core goods slightly negative. Headline CPI is seen at 0.37% m/m and 3.4% y/y on higher energy and food.

item.title: Canadian Dollar finds support from Oil surge despite Fed rate hike bets
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.3810 on Monday at the time of writing, down 0.15% on the day. The pair comes under some pressure as the sharp rise in Oil prices supports the Canadian Dollar (CAD), although underlying strength in the US Dollar (USD) limits the downside.

item.title: Euro area: Inflation overshoot extends ECB hiking path – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale economists Anatoli Annenkov, Michel Martinez and colleagues expect Euro area inflation to stay above target beyond 2027, with headline inflation projected to peak near 3.7-3.8% and core around 2.7-2.8%.

item.title: Asia FX: Oil shock keeps tone cautious – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong expects Asia ex-Japan (AxJ) currencies to start the week on a selectively cautious footing after renewed US–Iran tensions lifted Brent above US$96.

item.title: Euro benefits from weaker US Dollar as ECB decision looms
item.description: EUR/USD holds modest gains at the start of North American trading hours on Monday as a softer US Dollar (USD) and stronger-than-expected Eurozone Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data support the Euro (EUR).

item.title: Euro: ECB tightening supports currency – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad expects the European Central Bank (ECB) to deliver another 25 bps hike this week, taking the policy rate to 2.50%, supported by above-target Eurozone inflation and a firmer growth outlook.

item.title: US Dollar: Range-bound support as Fed priced – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes that resilient global equities and an above-consensus US jobs report mean the Dollar should be stronger, but risk appetite is capping gains. He highlights upcoming US CPI and Treasury auctions as key catalysts.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Six-month lows at the 209.20 area under pressure
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) has resumed its bearish trend against a stronger Japanese Yen (JPY) on Monday, as comments from Japanese officials hinting at a steeper Bank of Japan (BoJ) monetary tightening cycle have provided a fresh boost to the Yen.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Trade tensions and US CPI in focus – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities notes that a data-light week in Canada will keep attention on CAN-US trade tensions as Canadian countertariffs take effect. The US has already signalled higher tariffs on Canadian vehicles from January 1.

item.title: Brent: Uptrend targets $102 before higher projections - Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts highlight that Brent has resumed a steady advance after defending its 200-DMA in August and crossing a multi-month descending trend line.

item.title: Indian Rupee remains higher despite oil strain, hawkish Fed bets
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) gains against the US Dollar (USD) at the start of the week.

item.title: US Dollar: CPI holds key after jobs-driven support – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong notes that stronger US payrolls initially lifted the US Dollar (USD) and US Dollar Index (DXY), but softer wage growth and only modest Fed repricing capped gains.

item.title: Saudi Oil facilities hit in fresh strikes, WTI surges above $90
item.description: According to the Financial Times, Saudi Aramco’s Oil facilities in Jizan were hit on Monday. The extent of the damage is currently being assessed, the newspaper reported.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Remains sticky to 20-day EMA
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is marginally higher to near 1.1625 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Monday. The major currency pair trades broadly sideways amid an extended weekend in the United States (US) due to Labor Day.

item.title: Silver slips below $66 as strong NFP report revives Fed rate hike bets
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades under pressure on Monday, falling 0.79% on the day to around $65.70 at the time of writing.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Testing support at previous highs in the 0.8585 area
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is trading lower against the British Pound (GBP) following mixed Eurozone macroeconomic figures on Monday. The EUR/GBP pair is testing support at a previous resistance area, at 0.8585 ahead of the US session opening, after failing to find acceptance above the 0.8600 area last week.

item.title: 154.06: Japanese Yen hits fresh six-month highs amid hopes of steeper BoJ hikes
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) resumes its uptrend against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, as the dust from a bright US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report settles, and Japanese officials hint at some steepening of the Bank of Japan’s (BoJ) tightening cycle ahead.

item.title: Euro tumbles as Japanese Yen benefits from BoJ rate hike bets
item.description: EUR/JPY falls 1.11% on Monday and trades around 179.45 at the time of writing. The sharp decline in the cross mainly reflects the strong appreciation of the Japanese Yen (JPY), supported by growing expectations of monetary policy tightening by the Bank of Japan (BoJ).

item.title: EM FX: Policy holds shape CLP, PLN, PEN, TRY – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad expects Chile, Poland, Peru and Türkiye to keep policy rates unchanged at upcoming meetings.
